cards.text: Judah's king Jehoiakim did evil in the sight of the LORD, and now his son Jehoiachin reigns in his place in Jerusalem. His mother is Nehushta, daughter of Elnathan, from right there in Jerusalem. The new king is eighteen years old with a WHOLE KINGDOM on his shoulders, friend, and I can't carry two cookie boxes without my mustache filing a complaint.

cards.question: Eighteen-year-old Jehoiachin becomes king of Judah. He reigns in Jerusalem for three ___.
Just like his father Jehoiakim, King Jehoiachin does evil in the sight of the LORD.

cards.text: Three months on the throne isn't a reign, friend, it's a FREE TRIAL. And at that time, the servants of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, march up to Jerusalem.

cards.question: The servants of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, have marched up to Jerusalem. What happens to the city?

answers.text: It pays them to go home
It sends out its army to fight

cards.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar comes to the city himself, while his servants are still besieging it. You know it's serious when the boss stops sending emails and shows up at your desk with his coat still on.

cards.question: Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, is at Jerusalem himself. What does King Jehoiachin do?

answers.text: He surrenders to the king of Babylon
He sneaks out of the city at night
He rides out to fight the king of Babylon

cards.question: Jehoiachin surrenders to the king of Babylon all by himself, while his mother and his officials stay out of it.

cards.text: So the king of Babylon takes Jehoiachin captive, and then Nebuchadnezzar turns his eyes to the house of the LORD and the royal palace. Friend, I KNOW that look, because it's how every hand looked reaching into my old junk drawer on cleanout day.

cards.question: At the house of the LORD and the royal palace, Nebuchadnezzar leaves the treasures right where they are.
Long ago, Solomon, king of Israel, made gold articles in the temple of the LORD. What does Nebuchadnezzar do with them?

answers.text: He leaves them in the temple
He hands them to his servants

cards.text: Here's the thing, friend: Nebuchadnezzar carrying off those treasures happens just as the LORD had declared.

Then he carries all Jerusalem into exile: the commanders, the mighty men of valor, the craftsmen and the metalsmiths, TEN THOUSAND captives in all. Ten THOUSAND, friend, let that one sit in the oven a second.

cards.question: The commanders, the mighty men, the craftsmen and the metalsmiths are all taken from Jerusalem. Who stays behind in the land?

cards.text: Jehoiachin goes to Babylon too, with his mother, his wives, his officials and the leading men of the land, and the king of Babylon also takes seven thousand men of valor and a thousand craftsmen and metalsmiths. That's not a raid, friend, that's a rival bakery walking out the door with every baker who can actually BAKE.

cards.question: The seven thousand men of valor and the thousand craftsmen and metalsmiths taken to Babylon are all strong and fit for ___.
With Jehoiachin gone, the king of Babylon makes Mattaniah, Jehoiachin's ___, king in his place.

cards.text: Then the king of Babylon changes Mattaniah's name to Zedekiah. When I got my fresh start, the ONE thing I asked for was to keep my name, so believe me, I'd be holding that name tag with both ends of my mustache.
And that's where we set this batch down for now, friend. Trust me, Judah's story is not done yet.

findings.problem: Card 9 says Nebuchadnezzar 'turns his eyes to the house of the LORD and the royal palace' and compares it to hands reaching into the drawer on cleanout day. That tells the baker he is about to strip both places, which gives away card 10's answer (whether he leaves the treasures where they are).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: In the backstory, the drawer's cleanout never happened. The drawer friends only feared it might, and Papa Dorin was called out before anything like that came. Saying every hand reached into 'my old junk drawer on cleanout day' adds a new event to his backstory.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The joke image doesn't hold together. 'I KNOW that look, because it's how every hand looked' gives a hand a look, so the line doesn't click on first read.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Card 19 is only the 'story isn't over' line and tells nothing from the passage, but it cites 2 Kings 24:17. The citation rule says a card cites the verses it tells, and this card tells none.
findings.question: What should a story card cite when it holds only the 'story isn't over' line and no passage content: the last verse of the passage, null, or something else?
